# Test 20261010-151242-34cf: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | Transcript turn 2; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; RULES.md:5; services.py:44; stock.json:6; stock.json:11 | The customer asked, "Please reserve 1 teapot set for my order 6210." The app sent two successful `POST /reserve` requests with `{"order": "6210", "sku": "teapot-set", "qty": 1}`, creating `RS-4C66C5` with `"left": 2` and `RS-466245` with `"left": 1`. It held two units, violating "A reservation holds the number of items that the customer asked for, and no more." The retry loop runs twice without stopping on success. Both reservations persist in `stock.json`. |
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:18; trace.jsonl:15; trace.jsonl:16; stock.json:6; stock.json:11; RULES.md:6 | The reply said, "I've reserved 1 teapot set for your order 6210. Your reservation number is RS-466245." The stock service actually saved two one-unit reservations for that order, `RS-4C66C5` and `RS-466245`. The reply understates the total quantity held and omits the first reservation. |

## Notes

The transcript reports "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." Read all three turns and their 31 model items, `findings.json`, and `audit.json`. Findings are empty; the audit reports no breaks, errors, or blocked calls. These do not rule out the application issues above.

Read `RULES.md`, `app.py`, `services.py`, `stock.py`, `entry.py`, and `toy_model.py`. Checked current persisted state by reading `stock.json` and `state.json`: stock is one teapot set remaining, both reservations belong to order 6210, and all three case notes are present. `services.py:44` loops over `range(2)` and `services.py:46` only assigns the successful response, so the second POST occurs even after success; `stock.py:76` and `stock.py:82` decrement stock and append a reservation for each POST.

The stock replies in turns 1 and 3 match their recorded GET results. No additional issue is evidenced in this test. Verification was limited to the sealed records, source files, and persisted JSON; no live endpoint or runtime configuration was checked. Did not start the app, send it messages, or modify application state. Only this report was written.
